batch_strategy: Supplement the pending 16 with targeted tests of loading-dependent endpoint behavior, unresolved solvent-response shape, and structural transfer. Include two previously unobserved molecules and several low-retention or predicted-reversal probes. Freeze these 16 IDs together with the pending 16 and retain the packet's supplied premeasurement predictions unchanged before any label reveal.

choices.reason: Measure m177 at 50/1, 100 uL, predicted 12.69/70.31 mL. At the same solvent ratio, 50 uL measured 21.33/59.88 (5b706e17e8412d02342f), whereas 150 uL measured 4.49/81.30 (b514312eda7950cdcf1c). The intermediate loading tests whether the model's interpolated onset and completion are justified or whether the discrepancy is irregular. This is a direct test of a large observed loading-associated difference.

Measure m177 at 1/1, 150 uL, predicted 4.83/20.35 mL. Matched 2/1 and 5/1 observations are 4.82/10.90 and 4.99/20.42 (bef81d4dd93af26c12a9, 76643e968ecc935c745c). The model now predicts a completion dip at 2/1. This stronger-eluent anchor tests whether broad weak-eluent corrections have distorted the beginning of the curve.

Measure m45 at 10/1, 100 uL, predicted 23.09/48.58 mL. Matched 5/1 and 20/1 labels are 9.81/18.46 and 26.49/57.16 (fc47eff9bc6b7be6c207, e6605c23fb1943a6b848). The new 50/1 record 129036e0bccc4ff7e848 has negative completion and reversed endpoint order, so it cannot establish a physical retention collapse. This intermediate measurement tests the valid part of the response and helps constrain its shape despite that anomalous record.

Measure ortho-methoxyacetophenone m127 at 5/1, 150 uL, predicted 15.53/21.19 mL. The model predicts an onset peak relative to its selected 10/1 row and the measured 20/1, 150-uL result of 5.08/31.97 (ebdeaba52880c7eade16). Together with the 2/1, 100-uL anchor fd8b5ea3b704959cd1ab, this tests a poorly constrained, nonmonotonic segment rather than assuming a conventional curve.

Measure m127 at 10/1, 150 uL, predicted 10.53/35.32 mL, paired with the selected 5/1 row at identical loading conditions. The matched 20/1 observation ebdeaba52880c7eade16 finishes at 31.97 mL, while 50/1 at 50 uL finishes at 23.65 (52b9af4df1f1e7cd4d9b). This tests the predicted intermediate completion maximum and distinguishes a supported local response from interpolation artifacts; the 50/1 comparison remains loading-confounded.

Measure cyano-benzophenone m159 at 1/1, 100 uL, predicted 6.32/19.76 mL. The model predicts earlier completion at 2/1, while observed pure EA at 50 uL gives 3.59/8.86 (6c27c0ab37bb8d812822) and matched 10/1 gives 7.76/30.39 (c6e78c97267cbb98dc22). A strong-eluent anchor tests whether the large observed weak-eluent response has been propagated too broadly across the curve and complements the nitro-benzophenone experiment.

Measure m155 at 5/1, 50 uL. Its prediction is internally inconsistent: V1 10.53 exceeds V2 7.14 mL. The newly measured same-loading 50/1 anchor is 8.08/10.58 (42858a5819b8eb812861). This tests the unconstrained stronger-eluent segment and supplies a valid endpoint pair in a fluorinated aromatic region that also connects to pending m156. The predicted inversion is a model failure, not an observed chromatographic reversal.

Measure dibenzalacetone m164 in pure EA, 100 uL, predicted 1.57/19.28 mL. Matched 1/1, 20/1, and 50/1 observations are 5.12/10.05, 13.35/35.72, and 28.20/68.68 (3f6b817d855e67b3b406, b7fffd840d208b29776c, c9bef93a79964dc6ede1). The predicted broadening in pure EA is untested. This endpoint of the solvent range can distinguish a real strong-solvent effect from a learned extrapolation artifact.

Measure dimethyl acetylenedicarboxylate m91 at 5/1, 100 uL, predicted 6.20/9.14 mL. Recent 20/1 and 50/1 labels finish near 13.5 mL (bc98537714d620facf79, 48679ae48dd485ffb7a6); the latter was overpredicted by 23.66 mL at acquisition. This stronger-eluent point tests whether the repaired shallow response extends across conditions and helps distinguish this diester from strongly retained multifunctional esters. Existing anchors have different sample volumes, which remain covariates.

Measure acetophenone oxime m11 at 10/1, 100 uL, predicted 9.20/23.64 mL. Its matched 5/1 label is 6.93/15.70 (1182373ab8814dbe2f43), 20/1 at 50 uL is 20.68/45.58 (79cb1738d945317e5bfa), and matched 50/1 is 43.11/119.20 (9ffee2813aef5c26f96f). This fills the transition between modest and substantial retention in a donor/acceptor environment distinct from alcohols and ketones, where historical errors changed sign across solvent ratios.

Measure previously unobserved dibromonaphthalene m5 at 50/1, 100 uL, predicted 3.20/16.52 mL. Maximum observed similarity is 0.524. Bromonaphthalene m7 and bromophenanthrene m4 have measured weak-eluent anchors (96e2b82e29c9f4fe8548 is not used as an analogue; relevant observations are ba5381d85ba24754040c and 42b3b7216aee53ebe1cc). This adds a connected test of ring size and halogen substitution in donor-free aromatics, where early onset need not imply a short completion interval.

Measure previously unobserved m50 at 50/1, 50 uL, predicted 6.87/10.01 mL; maximum observed similarity is 0.346. This branched benzylic-side-chain chloride extends coverage beyond the observed linear phenylalkyl halides, including m148 at 50/1 (7bdb81ebd10a45bc8ad1) and m1 at 50/1 (24bf82db0ce55835b608). The label tests transfer of low-retention predictions across branching and halogen environment, with different loading masses retained explicitly.

Measure m169 at 50/1, 100 uL, predicted 21.80/52.04 mL. Its observed 1/1 anchor is 4.92/9.65 (334348368030ba5ce3b6), leaving the weak-eluent response uncovered. Related chloroalkyl aryl ketone m170 measures 14.23/31.30 at 50/1 (98f7b4e7c44ba0532e85), while m68's recent weak-eluent label was much shallower than predicted. This tests transfer involving ring fluorination and side-chain length; neither feature can be isolated causally by this comparison.

Measure acetylfluorene m38 at 10/1, 50 uL, predicted 18.39/38.60 mL. Its matched 20/1 anchor is 30.86/58.61 (cace6f00c46aea69fe39), and 2/1 at 100 uL is 4.82/12.63 (a2f5638c0f2528673e4e). Pending m40 at 10/1, 50 uL supplies a connected acetylnaphthalene comparison. This tests where retention growth begins across fused aromatic carbonyl scaffolds without assuming the pending outcome.

Measure trifluoromethoxyphenol m209 in pure EA, 100 uL, predicted 4.05/11.84 mL. Its 1/1, 50-uL observation is 5.22/9.61 (cbe7e55b0a4f7b4c2a2), and 5/1, 150 uL is 7.45/17.05 (edfbbb86c05a0aeb1bfb). This tests the predicted strong-eluent completion reversal in a phenol without an adjacent carbonyl. Salicylaldehyde's measured broad pure-EA interval (ff3ee95fed58907ff8b3) is a useful contrast, not proof that the behavior transfers.

Measure terephthalaldehyde m191 at 5/1, 50 uL, predicted 4.33/36.02 mL. Observed 2/1 at 150 uL is 7.07/23.74 (53becf1a41d72abcc45a), and 10/1 at 100 uL is 27.27/61.62 (bae9d67e095423d8edd2). The prediction places early onset beside a growing completion volume at the missing intermediate ratio. This tests transition placement and endpoint decoupling in a dialdehyde, while acknowledging the loading differences.

hypotheses.content: m177 exhibits substantial loading-associated differences in weak eluent, including changes in onset and completion in opposite directions. The discrepancy extends beyond the formerly anomalous 20/1 observation, but a smooth loading law and a causal mechanism remain unestablished.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: A model that nearly ignores loading can average incompatible endpoint pairs and propagate the resulting response across related aromatic carbonyls. A loading interpolation and a strong-eluent anchor constrain different parts of this failure.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At 50/1, does 100 uL interpolate between the 50- and 150-uL endpoints, and does the 150-uL strong-eluent curve really have a completion dip at 2/1?

hypotheses.content: m45 has a substantial measured rise from 5/1 to 20/1, but the previous hypothesis of a conventional weak-eluent curve cannot be evaluated from its new 50/1 record: that record has negative V2 and V2 below V1. Its origin is unknown, and it should not be interpreted as evidence for physical early elution.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The anomalous recorded target can distort a sparsely observed acid curve. A valid intermediate label can constrain the learnable relationship without inventing a meaning for the anomalous measurement or changing the supplied data.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does matched-loading 10/1 support the predicted rapid rise between the valid 5/1 and 20/1 anchors?

hypotheses.content: Aromatic carbonyl response shapes depend on structural environment. Recent fluoro- and bromoacetophenone labels support positional differences but weaken the predicted shallow para-fluoro response; the shallow m68 response further argues against a common upward correction. Some methoxy-carbonyl curves remain nonmonotonic or poorly constrained.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Local solvent pairs and comparisons to pending carbonyl measurements can teach which structural changes alter onset, completion, or curve shape, rather than fitting a family-wide retention offset.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Are m127's predicted intermediate maxima real, and do the unmeasured m169 and m38 response segments follow their predicted growth?

hypotheses.content: Large weak-eluent errors require endpoint-specific and solvent-local corrections. Strong-eluent anchors can remain accurate after large weak-eluent failures, while predicted reversals and intermediate onset dips require direct testing rather than enforced monotonic interpretation.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Labels at missing strong- and intermediate-eluent segments can prevent extreme observations from shifting whole curves and can teach separate onset and completion responses across functional groups.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do m159, m164, m209, and m191 exhibit their predicted reversals or endpoint decoupling, and where does the oxime response begin to rise?

hypotheses.content: The new m155 weak-eluent anchor leaves its stronger-eluent response unconstrained, and the current model still produces inverted onset/completion predictions at 5/1. A new label can repair this local structural transfer failure.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The observed 50/1 interval is valid, whereas the candidate prediction violates endpoint ordering. Measuring the same loading at another ratio tests whether a single new-molecule anchor has produced an unreliable condition response.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At 5/1 and 50 uL, what valid endpoint pair replaces the predicted 10.53/7.14 mL inversion?

hypotheses.content: Multiple ester groups or high polar surface area do not by themselves imply a steep solvent response. m91's recent weak-eluent labels resemble a shallow-response regime, and transfer from strongly retained multifunctional esters needs condition-specific checks.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The Row distribution contains both shallow and steep ester responses. A stronger-eluent m91 label can help prevent descriptor-driven overprediction from returning after retraining on high-retention examples.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m91 remain in the predicted low-retention regime at 5/1, consistent with its measured 10/1–50/1 range after accounting for loading?

feedback_interpretation: The latest results strengthen endpoint-specific repair and make loading a concrete priority for m177. Its 150-uL 10/1 completion was underpredicted by 24.18 mL; at 50/1, onset was overpredicted by 17.33 mL while completion was underpredicted by 21.94 mL. Thus the discrepancy is broader than one unusual 20/1 point. Conversely, m60 at 2/1 and m118 at 2/1 were closely predicted, supporting localized response corrections rather than blanket upward shifts. m206 at 1/1 was overpredicted, and m99 at 5/1 had accurate onset with modest completion overprediction, so I reduce emphasis on further simple alcohol anchors this round. Para-fluoroacetophenone's 50/1 completion was underpredicted by 16.42 mL, whereas m68's was overpredicted by 9.86 mL; these outcomes reinforce structural specificity. The m45 50/1 result is an anomalous recorded target, not evidence that the acid physically elutes at negative volume, and it weakens the prior curve hypothesis without establishing an alternative mechanism. Pending-CW feedback independently identified substantial m91 completion overprediction, motivating a stronger-eluent check. m155 and m151 were reasonably predicted at 50/1, but m155's current stronger-eluent endpoint inversion warrants follow-up. The authoritative table also corrects the previous m99 rationale: its 2/1, 50-uL anchor is 30456dafbfe681b5af70, while 304fb0fdb486ae4b7a07 is m19. All stated errors are acquisition-time errors, not current residuals.
batch_rationale: The pending batch already covers several ester, ether, nitrile, phenol, and substituted-carbonyl segments. These supplements add information that those rows will not directly provide: m177 tests loading interpolation and possible propagation of weak-eluent corrections into strong eluent; m45 constrains a valid response segment beside an anomalous target; the m127 pair tests an entire disputed local shape; and m155 addresses a current endpoint-ordering failure. Additional oxime, dialdehyde, cyano-benzophenone, conjugated-ketone, phenol, and diester measurements test transition placement and predicted reversals across connected chemical environments. m38 connects directly to pending acetylnaphthalene, while m169 tests a sparsely anchored haloalkyl ketone response. The two previously unobserved molecules extend low-retention structural coverage through meaningful analogues. This combination can improve generalization across both modest- and high-retention rows without assuming that high predicted volumes or broad elution intervals are intrinsically valuable. Nearly identical loading variants and duplicate-condition rows were generally avoided; loading comparisons were retained where measured discrepancies justify them. Quantile widths are treated as uncalibrated single-model outputs, and their crossings preclude a simple uncertainty ranking. Missing experimental variables and variability limit causal attribution.
